correctness.rationale: From chi(xh)=chi(x), det(h)=1 and tr(xh)=tr(x). In characteristic 2 the SL2 Cayley-Hamilton identity h+h^{-1}=tr(h)I, paired with x, forces tr(h)=0 when tr(x) is nonzero, hence h^2=I and H is an elementary abelian 2-group embedded in the centralizer of a nontrivial nilpotent, size <=q. For tr(x)=0, A=span(H) is a unital algebra in x-perp. If dim A=3, then A-perp=span(x) and tr(xab)=0 implies xa in span(x) for every a, so A would be scalar: contradiction. Thus dim A<=2, so commutative. The three quadratic algebra types yield determinant-one group sizes q-1, q, q+1; full field norm-one torus attains q+1 with x Frobenius. This checks all field sizes q=2^e uniformly, including q=2 and scalar subcase.
